Capture It - Game Features Script

Capture It is a friends-only creative video-making game where players can create, film, and share all kinds of content.

Players can make movies, videos, Shorts, animations, roleplays, and livestreams all within one platform.

The movie editor allows users to build stories scene by scene. Players can choose thumbnails, add sounds, place characters, set poses, adjust camera angles, and fully control how each scene looks and feels.

Filming takes place across a variety of built-in maps such as cities, schools, castles, beaches, and forests. Players also have the ability to build their own maps or copy existing ones and customize them freely.

Capture It includes a wide range of free extensions. These include AI Summaries, the BrightUp Thumbnail Editor, a Video Title Generator, a Thumbnail Tester, additional video assets, and special packs like the Pirate Pack. No Robux is required to access these tools.

Players can enhance their videos using many different assets such as trees, sharks, ocean items, plants, rocks, pirate props, furniture, and visual effects to make each scene more detailed and unique.

Captions can be enabled so viewers can read dialogue and chat clearly, even when audio is not available.

Profiles can be customized with banners, playlists, connected videos, favorite creations, and featured thumbnails to showcase a creator's work.

Videos can be promoted to help reach a larger audience and grow visibility. Promoted videos can be skipped instantly by viewers.

The game also includes copyright protection tools to help safeguard original creations. Reports are reviewed to maintain fairness and support a creative community.

In addition to creation tools, players can enjoy mini games or use special maps as filming locations for their projects.

Capture It is built around creativity, storytelling, and sharing-giving players everything they need to create and express their ideas.

answers.ask: Each built-in set has its own setting - is there a house style tying them together, or should each be built in its own register?
answers.answer: Each set should use its own matching register—city, school, castle, beach, and forest should look distinct—but keep a clean, accessible Roblox creative-tool style across all of them.

answers.ask: Which set should be built first, and should they share one world or be separate places?
answers.answer: Build the city set first, since it is the most flexible starting filming location. Keep the sets as separate selectable places so each can be loaded cleanly for filming.

answers.ask: How large should each filming set be? A set built for camera work is usually smaller than a playable map.
answers.answer: Keep each set compact and built for camera work: a small, dense collection of recognizable filming areas rather than a large explorable map.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: Each built-in set has its own setting - is there a house style tying them together, or should each be built in its own register? A: Each set should use its own matching register—city, school, castle, beach, and forest should look distinct—but keep a clean, accessible Roblox creative-tool style across all of them.
- [author] shape — Q: Which set should be built first, and should they share one world or be separate places? A: Build the city set first, since it is the most flexible starting filming location. Keep the sets as separate selectable places so each can be loaded cleanly for filming.
- [author] scale — Q: How large should each filming set be? A set built for camera work is usually smaller than a playable map. A: Keep each set compact and built for camera work: a small, dense collection of recognizable filming areas rather than a large explorable map.
- [agent_inferred] city composition — Q: Which plain city areas should the first compact set contain? A: Use one short street intersection, sidewalks, generic exterior facades, and one alley, with no enterable interiors until requested.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a library of five separate compact filming sets—City, School, Castle, Beach, and Forest—each loaded as its own place and each using a distinct matching visual register within one clean, accessible block-based creative-tool style. Make the City set first and authoritative: one small dense exterior block containing a short street intersection, sidewalks, generic urban facades, and one alley, arranged as several recognizable camera-ready compositions rather than a large explorable map. Keep buildings as exterior set facades with no invented interiors. The other four places remain compact school, castle, beach, and forest filming sets. Exclude editors, profile screens, captions, menus, extensions, promotion tools, and other UI from the geometry.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Entertainment because these environments are selectable filming sets built to be composed and consumed through a camera rather than won.

## Shape and preset
Use `space-staged`, Zone (Lobby and Isolated Stage), as a container for five genuinely separate selectable set maps, with no physical lobby required. Each set uses `set-display`, Zone (Display Set), because it is operated as a compact camera set rather than traversed as a large playable world. No single Entertainment preset covers a multi-set creative library, so the preset is none.

## Config requirements
Use `settlement-density` for the City set's dense exterior block, `path-street` from Roleplay & Avatar Sim for its street-and-sidewalk circulation, and `vignette-photo` for the several camera-ready compositions within each compact set. The school, castle, beach, and forest registers are scene-specific image geometry. Do not apply `building-interior` to the facade-only first City build.

## Layout requirements
No post-segmentation trigger, collectible, spawn, NPC, portal, or editor-control placement is established. Characters, props, poses, cameras, thumbnails, sounds, captions, and visual effects are creation mechanics and user-placed content rather than fixed layout.

## Layout components
The `space-staged` container has exactly five map segments: City, School, Castle, Beach, and Forest. Each is a compact `set-display` with its own theme. City is the first authoritative segment and contains one street intersection, sidewalks, generic facades, one alley, and several camera-ready angles. The other four segments remain small dense sets in their named registers, each with an independent boundary and no cross-map surface.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: the City set's camera-ready facade composition leads, and each simple compact set plan can be projected afterward.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale is small per set because camera work needs dense recognizable areas rather than large traversal. Themes are distinct city, school, castle, beach, and forest registers under a clean accessible creative-tool style. Modifier `P4` is required for five separate selectable maps, and `SET` applies because these are filming sets operated by camera and character-placement tools rather than avatar traversal spaces.
